result.summary: Disconnect connected callbacks in the signal destructor within btcsignals. This ensures surviving connection handles report disconnected and any captured callback state is released upon signal destruction.
result.problem: When a connection handle outlives its signal, a callback that remains connected at signal destruction is not released, leaking captured state and causing the surviving handle to erroneously report that it is still connected.
evidence: Identified in review of preceding PR #36011: 'destroying the signal still did not disconnect its callbacks automatically, as pointed out by the author in this #36011 comment' (description)

PR commit message explains that 'If a connection handle is still connected when its signal is destroyed, it outlives the signal and the handle keeps the callback alive and continues to report that it is connected' (commit 1a0f15f45a)
result.scope_notes: Small follow-up to merged PR #36011 covering signal destruction cleanup in btcsignals and associated unit tests.
result.card: Disconnect callbacks automatically when a signal is destroyed in btcsignals, and update unit tests accordingly. Previously, if a connection handle outlived the signal, connected callbacks remained alive with captured state and the handle falsely reported connected. This follows up on merged PR #36011 to handle the implicit destruction case identified during its review.

risk.why: A bug in signal disconnection during destruction could cause a crash or lifetime mismanagement in internal event signaling.
